articleTitle: Barriers and motives experienced by manufacturing companies in implementing circular economy initiatives: The case of manufacturing industry in Slovakia
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article reacts on the knowledge gap regarding implementation of circular economy (CE) initiatives across manufacturing companies worldwide, but particularly in Slovakia. It analyzes which barriers to which extent are Slovak companies experiencing while implementing CE initiatives and what are the major motives to implement these initiatives. The data presented in this article has been obtained through research of innovations in manufacturing companies in Slovakia. This research was part of a wider European Manufacturing Survey (EMS) in 2018. Results regarding differences in experiencing the barriers in small and big (+middle) companies shows, that there are no differences in means (on α = 0,05) and representation of different answers is very similar, except some partial differences in economic barriers, legislative barriers and risk in business model barrier. Correlation analysis shows no relation between size of companies and degree of experienced barriers. Regarding the motives, there are significant differences in percentage of companies in group of small and group of large (+middle) companies, which are motivated by regulation compliant and cost saving motives.

articleTitle: Recycling of lithium accumulators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: More than 200,000 tons of portable batteries and accumulators are placed on the market annually in the EU countries and more than 20 wt. % of them are lithium ones. In addition to lithium, they contain metals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper aluminum and others. High share of lithium battery and a limited lifespan results to a large quantities of waste. Pyrometallurgical recycling methods, which are currently more widely used, have a lower selectivity and consist only in the recovery of selected metals. The remaining substances are concentrated in slag, which is deposited in landfills. Lithium slag composition and leaching behavior of lithium and cobalt in Sulfuric acid was studied in this paper. The leaching was carried out in 0.1, 0.5, 1 and 2M H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with and without 30 ml of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at temperatures of 20, 40, 60 and 80°C. All slag samples were leached for 90 minutes with constant stirring of 300rpm at liquid to solid ratio of 50. The obtained results showed that 66.85% of Co and 99% of Li was leached at 1M H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with addition of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at temperature of 80°C.

articleTitle: Agroecological Aspects of Cultivation Shiitake Mushroom in Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Shiitake mushroom (Lentinula edodes (Berk.) Pegl.) is currently the second mostly cultivated mushroom in the world. It's valued for its exotic taste, flavor and nutritional value. The aim of our work is complex analysis of agroecological aspects of cultivation Lentinula edodes. There are two main cultivation techniques - growing on logs and on sawdust substrate. Cultivation on logs is considered traditional in Far East (Japan, China, Korea, etc.) and cultivation on sawdust substrate is new and very popular in USA, Europe. In Ukraine shiitake is still novelty, only a few farms are growing this mushroom. Main challenges for Ukrainian growers are: choosing of right cultivation technique, need of introduction of the product to local consumers, price support and ensures the profitability of production. The article provides general information about shiitake mushroom, growing techniques and cultivation in Ukraine.

articleTitle: Microclimate and thermal comfort parameters simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper deals with the simulation of microclimatic conditions in the indoor environment and their influence on the perception of thermal comfort of man. It contains an overview of available simulation tools for analysis of microclimatic conditions, their principles and utilization. The experimental part of the paper includes measurement of air temperature, air velocity and relative humidity at the selected workplace and subsequent use of selected simulation tools for interpretation of results. Based on the simulation results, it is possible to monitor the exceeding values of the selected parameters and optimize the microclimate conditions in the workplace to the most effective compliance with the legislative, hygienic and safety requirements.

articleTitle: Continuous Acoustic Monitoring of Railroad Network in the Czech Republic Using Smart City Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Due to the high density of settlements in the Czech Republic, freight rail corridors are led through populated areas. Tracks are still dominated by noisy cars braked with metal brake blocks, which in the course of passage cause several times higher noise than modern cars with non-metallic brakes. Although these are the technical parameters that determine the noise level of a train, it is not possible to find out of any registry the proportion of obsolete noisy vehicles on tracks. The long-term objective of the project is to identify individual problematic trains in terms of noise. In cooperation with national railroad authority, a system has been developed that utilizes the CESVA TA120 measuring sensor network and is designed to provide to the railroad operator, in addition to all the train parameters that can be traced (carrier, time, weight, length, number of vehicles and axles, video recordings) other essential information about the passing train - sound exposure level of the train pass. The plan is to build a sensor network using the existing infrastructure so that a detailed overview of the noise level of each single freight train can be obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of Human Factor Reliability in Workplace with Noise Load
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article presents an analysis of human reliability in the workplace with noise load. The noise load in the selected workplace is quantified within the article by measuring the standardized noise level of ISO 9612: 2009 Acoustics: Determination of occupational noise exposure, Technical method. The analysis of the reliability of the human factor at work, the aim of which is to identify possible human errors and their impact, is a systematic assessment of the factors influencing the manufacturing workers. The analysis includes identification of important sites affected by various errors caused by high noise load. The impact of noise on humans, especially in terms of the upper decibel scale or long-term exposure at the bottom of the decibel scale, leads to the organism loading and human failure during work. The probability of human error occurring in the selected workplace is estimated using the TESEO method.

articleTitle: Clinching and Clinch-Riveting as a Green Alternative to Resistance Spot Welding
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The automotive industry meets the requirements for increased safety, the regulations regarding environmental protection, and the requests of car drivers for more luxury features as well. Steel is the most essential material for car body production in the automotive industry. Hot-dip galvanizing is a standard procedure utilized to protect steels from corrosive environments. But low melting and boiling points of zinc create undesirable effects due to its evaporation during welding and formation of pores or cracks. The weld nuggets with sufficient quality made on galvanized steel sheets are realized by using longer weld times, higher electrode forces and higher welding currents. These increased values of welding parameters result in an increase in energy costs. Consequently, mechanical joining, especially clinching and clinch-riveting, has attracted more and more attention. The properties of the spot welded joints and the mechanical joints such as the clinched joints and the clinch-riveted joints of hot-dip galvanized steel sheets H220PD and DX51D were evaluated. The properties and quality of the joints were evaluated by the tensile test and the metallographic observation.

articleTitle: Green Synthesis of Irregular Shaped Gold Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: With the development of nanotechnology, a growing number of scientists going to apply the green chemistry to the synthesis of nanoparticles (NPs) and nanomaterials, because a bright future is predicted for a new field known as `green nano'. We expect several benefits of green chemistry applications: sustainability, cost-effectivity, low time consuming, and biocompatibility of new materials. The synthesis and application of nanomaterials have become a key technology in many more fields, such as medicine and pharmacy. These applications request not only control over the morphology of NPs but also their biocompatibility. Recent successes in the development of chemical methods for the synthesis of gold NPs have delivered a wide range of preparation tools. However, the effective control of morphology involves the utilization of toxic reducing agents (sodium borohydride, methoxy polyethylene glycol, potassium tartrate, and hydrazine), and stabilizers (sodium dodecyl benzyl sulfate, and polyvinylpyrrolidone). These factors limit the applications of the synthesized NPs. Therefore, extensive studies are directed on the development of green methods of NP synthesis. One possibility is the application of the biological approach, which means the synthesis of NPs using whole organisms or substances of biological origin. The present report will be focused on the analysis of recent successes in green synthesis of gold NPs with controlled size and shape.

Index Terms: Method For The Synthesis Of Nanoparticles

articleTitle: Impact of Natural Daylight for Human Comfort and Health
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: This article deals with influence of shortage of natural daylight at psychic and performance of workers and describes chances, how we can prevent this one negative influence. It provides a basic introduction to designing lighting to help designers create suitable lighting plans throughout the workday also addressing to management of companies to create a vital inter-section of functionality, health and aesthetics.

articleTitle: Granulation of Waste from Mineral Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The aim of this study was to find a suitable granulation method intended for the transformation of waste in powder form from nickel ore processing, into stable granules. Requirements for the granulate were a particle size of a few millimeters, high strength and low friability for trouble-free transportation and material handling. For their further use as a sorbent in bio-gas plants, the granules had to have high porosity. By applying non-compacting granulation methods, a granulate of the desired dimension and properties was created. The created granulates were analyzed by dynamic image analysis (DIA) and powder rheometer. A high shear granulation method was chosen as the best method for powder waste processing, in which the most sustainable granulates were created using a small amount of granulation liquid. The granules produced by this method had good strength, low friability and a porous structure.

articleTitle: Alkaline treatment of tin sludge
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Every industrial production is associated with waste production. Electrolytic tinning produces sludge containing approximately 57 % tin. Due to the limited tin reserves and its importance for industrial use, it is appropriate to treat this sludge. This work deals with hydrometallurgical treatment of tin sludge by alkaline leaching in sodium hydroxide solutions. Experiments show that the highest tin recovery of 90% was achieved using 3M NaOH at 80 °C. The next step after the leaching process is the refining of solution and electrolytic recovery of tin.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Bio-waste Processing and Design of Optimal System of Bio-waste Management in Selected Locality
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper deals with ways of recycling of bio-waste and at the same time deals with the proposal of optimal system of bio-waste management in selected locality. Theoretical background are based on basic concepts in the issue, as well as individual technologies and forms of recovery of bio-waste. The aim of the paper is to evaluate the situation of bio-waste processing. The constructional solution of bio-waste recovery consists in the design of the facility for the recovery itself. From the economic point of view, a detailed financial analysis for the time horizon of 3 years is elaborated.

articleTitle: Green Synthesis of Silver and Gold Nanoparticles Using Extract of Blackcurrant
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The presented study is dedicated to the green synthesis of stable gold and silver nanoparticles using natural polyphenols isolated from blackcurrant (Ribes nigrum L.) extract. A polyphenol fraction was prepared from the raw extract of blackcurrant fruits using solid-state extraction (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sub> reversed-phase). HPLC-DAD chromatography analyses have shown that the major components of used extract were anthocyanins (delphinidin-3-glucoside, delphinidin-3-rutinoside, cyanidin-3-glucoside, and cyanidin-3-rutinoside). Green protocol for the synthesis of gold and silver nanoparticles was developed through the optimization of reaction conditions (reactants ratio, pH of solutions, reaction time and temperature). The alkali conditions were observed to be necessary for the synthesis of highly mono-disperse spherical gold nanoparticles (diameter of 10 nm).

articleTitle: Analysis of input - output elements in the process of water jet technology and proposal the possibility of waste elimination
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of input-output elements in the process of using water jet technology. It analyses in detail the individual parts of the process, ie input, production and output in terms of analysis of logistic flows and the direction of the production process of the final product. It focuses on individual modules that can be tracked and edited. By implementing control modules in the production process, it is possible to prevent the generation of waste in the production process using the technology.

articleTitle: Drying of biological materials in the dryer with controlled vacuum chambers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Drying is a well-known technological process by which agricultural products are treated so as to be stored for longer times. Under the concept of drying are understood physical phenomena that, with the effect of heat, reduce the moisture content in the materials without a change in their chemical composition. Moisture is removed by condensation, evaporation or sublimation. The removal of moisture by methods other than by heat (e.g. mechanical or chemical) are not considered as drying. Agricultural materials in most cases represent biologically living organisms in their structure and composition of colloidal capillary-porous material. They contain a large number of microscopic pores, a microcapillary and a macrocapillary, in which water is able to pass from the inner to the grain surface or vice versa.

articleTitle: Method of determination of the boundary strength of pressed sheets of car bodies for categories over 1900 cm3
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Pressed steel sheets, in this case compacted vehicle bodies represent the structure diversity of the non-homogeneous material. There is necessity to determine the shear strength for the development of the construction of new processing equipment (cutting) of steel sheets. To calculate the shear strength it is necessary to know the ultimate firmness of the material. For homogeneous materials this parameter is normally available in the tables. The article discusses the experimental detection of boundary strength of pressed metal of vehicle bodies. To gain some relevant statistical evaluation the samples of the car body have been divided into three groups according to the engine capacity. The experiment was evaluated by the following statistical methods, analysis of variance using the AIC criterion and Grubbs test for outliers. According to the analysis of the measured parameters the resulting mathematical model, which is used for determination of optimal values of boundary strength, has been established. The resulting mathematical model can be used to determine the boundary strength, which serves as an input parameter for the calculation of shear strength required for the development of new equipment designed for the processing of scrap metal, with cutting.

articleTitle: A Concept of Environmental Monitoring System Based on Triboelectric Generator
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Today, the emergence of new technical means of monitoring the state of the environment based on modern approaches in the field of microcontroller technology is a tendency. First, it is necessary to emphasize the peculiarity of reducing the level of energy consumption for this type of devices, improving the quality of data communications (wireless communication), as well as the availability of components and their low cost in the market. An important feature of the effective functioning of the monitoring system is power sources. In this direction, the authors propose and develop new types of renewable energy converters, which are based on triboelectric and piezoelectric effects of ferroelectrics-semiconductors - Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> type.

articleTitle: Machinery Fire in Agriculture and its Impact on the Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Fires in agriculture are spreading rapidly (the rate of propagation depends on meteorological conditions), with large areas being hit and potentially threatening nearby buildings, equipment and stacks. Fires are difficult to access (limited load carrying capacity and throughput for mobile firefighting equipment) and can be extended to forest stands. There is often a lack of water to extinguish at the site of the fire, with water sources generally located at great distances. A part of the paper is also a description of the situation before the fire and ascertaining the causes of the fire. At the end of the article there is mentioned fire protection of machines with proposed protection of agricultural machines.

articleTitle: Enrofloxacin in Agroecosystems: Uptake by Plants and Phytotoxical Effect
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The fluoroquinolones are one of the most widely used classes of antibiotics. Enrofloxacin belongs to the class of fluoroquinolone antibiotics that have been intensively used for the treatment of bacterial infections in veterinary medicine. When antibiotic residues enter the soil, the main processes determining their persistence are sorption to organic particles and degradation. The article presents the results of studies on the sorption of enrofloxacin by different crops, provided that it's various concentrations in the soil (1000mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 100mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 10mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>). Experimental studies have shown that the activity of absorbed antibiotics depends on its concentration in the soil and species of an agricultural plant. It was found that the most active antibiotic absorbs Lactuca sativa var. Crispa and Calendula officinalis. The lowest content of enrofloxacin among the five plants was in Mentha piperita. Adding to the soil of enrofloxacin at a concentration of 1000 mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> leads to the formation of a high level of soil toxicity. In model ecosystems with Thymus serpillum and Mentha piperita, soil toxicity was more than 70%. The toxicity of enrofloxacin in the soil within In vivo experiments was on average 10% lower than in laboratory tests. The highest phytotoxic effect was observed in the soil of model ecosystems, where the concentration of enrofloxacin was 1000 mg·kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. It should be noted that in the soil where Lactuca sativa was grown, the phytotoxic effect was 56.17 % (In vitro) and 49.22% (In vivo). This is due to the active absorption of antibiotic by plants, which minimized the toxicity of the soil. The different terrestrial toxicological effects of enrofloxacin were studied using a series of bioassays and including sorption of fluoroquinolone antibiotic by five crop plants. Enrofloxacin is highly resistant, its biodegradation process is longer than other antibiotics, it is actively absorbed by the plants, and therefore it is necessary to control it content in phytoproduction.

articleTitle: Applications of Metal Hydride Materials for Hydrogen Compression
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article describes the compressor prototype which for hydrogen compression uses the chemical-thermal cycles of absorption and desorption of hydrogen into the intermetallic structure of metal. The used concept of a hydrogen compressor consists in the use of a suitable metal alloy which allows absorb hydrogen in its structure at low temperature and pressure. After heating up of alloy occurs to significant increase of pressure, what allows to compress hydrogen without its direct contact with moving parts. This principle of hydrogen compress provides safety of the process. The hydrogen compressor consists of a pair of tandem-connected metal hydride (MH) tanks with an integrated heat exchanger. The tanks are alternately heated and cooled whereby at the hydrogen absorption on one tank occurs to hydrogen desorption in second tank. Heat transport is made by heat pump for heating up and cooling is done, thanks to which saves considerable part of electricity.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of plastic deformation on the corrosion resistance of thin tin coated sheets
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Thin tin coated steel sheets are still one of the most used material in the production of packages. Majority of these sheets are processed by drawing. Decreasing thickness of the thin steel sheets and the increasing required speed of drawing in the production of packages often lead to the loss of stability of plastic deformation, which demonstrates itself through the localization of deformation or the material failure of processed packaging sheet. Localization of deformation significantly influences the change in thickness, the porosity of tin protection layer and its integrity. Two grades of tin coated steel sheets were used for the experimental research. Their properties were examined using uniaxial and biaxial tensile test. After the plastic deformation, the sheets were exposed to the corrosive environment and the influence of the size of deformation and the localization of deformation on the corrosion resistance of thin packaging sheets was evaluated. Some particular cases of corrosion of so called twist-off caps were analyzed as well.

articleTitle: The Device for a Reduction of Nutrients in Municipal Wastewater
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper focuses on the summation of existing approaches in a reduction of nitrogen and phosphorus content in municipal wastewater, as well as on the authors' own knowledge resulting from searching for unconventional approaches in water purification. It presents long-term measurements of wastewater quality by conventional methods and their confrontation with an unconventional electrolytic method, its laboratory and exterior experiments, together with their statistical and graphical evaluation. Finally, the possibilities of using this method in various areas are evaluated.

articleTitle: STEM in Natural Science Education in After-School Education
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Review of new and innovative approach in education, which integrate Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) and project based learning. The use of STEM in educational systems of different countries is considered. Effectivity and benefits of using STEM approach in pedagogical activity for learning are analyzed. Specific attention paid to possibilities of STEM in activity of after-school education. Thus, STEM in student learning is an important promising direction that promotes student development. The international community is paying close attention to the development and implementation of the STEM approach to school and university study, especially the United States of America. In article represented example of program with implementation of STEM approach for physical and mathematical workshops of after-school education. The need of further development of STEM approach consists in the competitiveness of education systems and the demands of modern society.

articleTitle: Copper Ions Adsorption Using Aminated Activated Carbons
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Here we report on the preparation of effective aminated sorbents based on activated carbon (AC), which was produced from natural raw material (Apricot pits) for the removal of heavy metal ions from wastewaters. For effective functionalization, bromination and following amination were carried out. At the amination stage, the grafted bromine groups were substituted by amino groups. Amination by ethylenediamine and monoethanolamine alcohol solutions can replace 0.52 mmol of bromine groups by 0.51-0.57 mmol of amino groups per gram of sorbent. We showed that the aminated ACs could remove 90% of Cu(II) ions from aqueous solutions containing from 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> to 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> mol/L of Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>. The regeneration of used sorbents and the recovery of copper were also studied to evaluate the reusability of the sorbents.

articleTitle: High-speed camera measurement of spinning rotor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: In the context of achieving the research objectives, the research team devoted itself to the planned activities throughout the year [1]. Depending on the spindle acceleration function over time, a dynamic trigger response is required when using the FEM feature. On this basis, it is possible to determine the technical and performance requirements for the spindle drive. For simulation results to match the true dynamic spindle response, the input values of the simulation model must be measured on the actual spindle. Therefore, based on real measurement, approximation of measured points, the initial curve was determined as input for the FEM model. It was necessary to perform a series of measurements of the initial spindle characteristic. The actual measurement data was then approximated to the initial curve for the simulation model. Based on the above steps, it is possible to predict the key technical requirements for the construction node. Spindle drive power requirements can be determined. Knowing the driving force and initial characteristics, it is possible to design alternatives to the technical structure of the spindle support structure and its drive. Only then will we choose the most appropriate from the possible design alternatives.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of hydrogen separator from synthesis gas using metal hydride alloys
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper deals with design of hydrogen separator from synthesis gas produced in plasma reactor by municipal waste treatment. The system uses metal hydride alloys, in particular La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,85</sub>Ce<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</sub>Ni<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> with a storage capacity of 1.43%, to separate hydrogen from the synthesis gas. The design consists of the design of the heating and cooling system of the metal hydride container, the measuring apparatus for monitoring temperatures, pressures and other relevant quantities that must be sensed to increase the efficiency of the device during its operation.

articleTitle: Testing the Effectiveness of Degreasing Agents
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper presents the results of testing the effectiveness of four types of degreasing agents for steel materials cleaning. Material contamination was simulated by applying a grease layer. Degreasing efficiency was tested at various time periods of degreasing by the weight method as well as by measuring the adhesion of the organic coating by several methods. The adhesion of the coating is closely related to the purity of the substrate. The result of the testing was to compile scores for individual degreasing agents and also to assess their environmental impact.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Sound Sources in a Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: In connection with a transfer of noise and vibrations into the internal space (interior) and external space (surroundings) of a vehicle, the acoustics are regarded as a construction component part of the development of vehicles. There is a growing emphasis placed the acoustic comfort. While the pragmatic, material and functional criteria had been crucial in the past, the emotional and feeling demands or wishes of a vehicle user are important today. The high level of a vehicle drive overall comfort is of a crucial importance for the occupants of the vehicle from the point of view of the drive comfort. Authors of the paper highlights the importance of acoustics for the drive comfort of the vehicle occupants from the point of view of the drive comfort perception. Authors emphasize the importance of acoustics for the drive comfort of vehicle occupants, noise-related statutory requirements, the conceptual conditions and they present the typical sources of vehicle sound.

articleTitle: Theoretical Estimation of Toxicity of New Condensed Heterocyclic Cationic Surfactants
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Estimation of toxicity of two new classes of heterocyclic condensed cationic surfactants was performed. The general synthetic approaches for obtaining the target heterocyclic systems of 1,2,4-triazole and thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine classes were discussed and the main routes to increasing of the chemical libraries through the efficient introduction of long-chain substituents were pointed out. The estimation of toxicity was done through: (a) the prediction of the LD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> values of acute rat oral toxicity with using GUSAR free online service; (b) the prediction of the LC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> values of fathead minnow with 96 hours exposure, which were predicted with using T.E.S.T. software. Computed LD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> and LC<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub> values testify that proposed heterocyclic surfactants have the toxicity rates close to the widely used surfactants like cetylpyridinium chloride, cetyltrimethylammonium bromide, and benzalkonium chloride. Consequently, target cationic surfactants of 1,2,4-triazole and thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine series can be considered as non-toxic detergents and will be synthesized for the next biological testing as disinfectants.

articleTitle: The Statistical Measurements of Photovoltaic Panels Degradation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper deals with the statistical verification of degradation of photovoltaic cells based on data from four photovoltaic power plants of different size and type of photovoltaic cells. The results of the course of statistical graphs, both multiplicative and cumulative, prove the truth of the theory of panel degradation over decades.

articleTitle: The Physical Environmental Factors in the Work Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The aim of this paper was to get more information about the influence of selected physical factors on humans at work. The paper presents the results of the experiment regarding the impact of selected physical factors on the work performance. The selected physical factors included noise, light and microclimate. Impact assessment of individual factors was performed by means of an Attention Test, namely a numerical rectangle, which was modified for easier readability. A short questionnaire was used to find out the experimental impressions that the participants filled out after the experiment ended. Thanks to the experiment and the questionnaire, it was possible to compare physical and mental perception of individual factors by the participants. We found that the worst-rated factor is noise. The factor that least influenced the work performance was microclimate.

articleTitle: Environmental Evaluation of Mechanical Engineering Products in their Conceptual Phase
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Design and development (D/D) procedures of mechanical engineering products (MEP-s) are explored holistically and are modelled by means of the sets system. The individual sets represent technical, economic, environmental, aesthetic and market requirements. The specific eco-design philosophy is derived from the environmental aspects and requirements. The final results of this process are environmentally compatible MEP-s. This philosophy is applied to the conceptual phase optimization of MEP-s. The described procedure is applied as a fundamental core for the software product CoDe-09 and its structure. An application in the automotive industry concludes the paper.

articleTitle: Contents of Professional Training of Future After-School Teachers in Pedagogical Universities of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article addresses the main issues of future teachers’ professional training after-school education system in Ukraine. The training of after-school teachers in pedagogical University discover on the example of the specialty “Secondary education (Design and Technology)” at the educational level of bachelor. Particular attention is paid to implementation of the content of training of future teachers of after-school education through the subjects of “After-school education pedagogy”, “Introduction to after-school education”, “History of technology”, “History of after-school education”, “Practic tools in after-school education”, “Theory and metods of teaching in workshops”, “Organizational and masswork of after-school institutions”, “Psychology of creative activity”, “Nanotechnology”, etc.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bioactive Fused Pyrimidines via Environmental Technologies
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Fused pyrimidines are important structural motifs in material science, medicinal chemistry, and are useful building blocks in organic synthesis. Herein we report a new approaches in preparation of condensed thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine-containing non-toxic compounds via environmentally friendly technologies. The microbiological activity of received compounds is also discussed.

articleTitle: Press machine with invert kinematic
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The briquetting is one of technologies which transforming biomass into biofuels with the required properties. We know three basic briquetting technologies - mechanical, hydraulic and screw. Screw press briquetting machine clearly produce the best-quality briquettes. The advantage of this sort of briquetting is that, as opposed to the other technologies, the briquettes are created continuously accordingly therefore are compactness, with high stiffness and densities. Average density of this kind of briquettes is 1.2-1.4 kg/dm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Briquettes can be produced in a deference of shapes and sizes. Current designs of the screw press briquetting machine have several structural drawbacks. Among them belong high wear of the screw tools, and low axial bearing durability. During starting produce briquettes at the screw press briquetting machine we have to heating of the rotating screw and during operation we have to cooling it. The result of our research has been in first stage a solution for removing faults in the existing constructions of screw press briquetting machine. It was a new design of briquetting presses with two screw “back to back” arrangement and with changeable front end sides of screw. In the second stage we have designed totally new conception of the construction and kinematics of the screw compactor (PP-5022-2015, or UV 7380). The essence of the proposed solution of the compacting machine with “inverted kinematics”. Aim of presented article is describe and develop function model of original construction for a compacting machine with inverted kinematics.

articleTitle: State assessment of stop gates of hydroelectric power plants
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: In the paper are described basic procedures that are necessary for analysis of deformation, strength, reliability and residual lifespan of stop gate (floodgate) equipment used in hydroelectric power stations. The structural analysis is realized by numerical and experimental methods of mechanics. Stop gate structures are very important parts of water power stations and their appropriate operation and reliability is crucial for whole power station. The analysis is at the beginning based on the finite element method and this computation serves for finding potentially critical locations in the structure. Those are then checked by experimental measurements. Further refinement of analysis is based on these basic steps. At the end of assessment, the recommendations for modification of structures in order to improve actual state are given.

articleTitle: An adsorption and desorption device for VOC
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The aim of this study was to perform a series of experiments with a new adsorption-desorption device. For adsorption of a volatile organic compound (in this study ethanol was chosen), 7 kinds of granulated activated carbon (GAC) were used. A matrix containing the volatile organic compound of 2 and 5 % aqueous stock solution of ethanol was used. In the device a gaseous phase of the matrix was adsorbed onto GAC (80g). The gaseous phase was acquired by stripping the stock solution with an air blower. The adsorbed gaseous phase was desorbed from GAC by high temperature. The desorbed molecules were condensed in the next part of the device and accumulated in a two-neck round bottom flask at the end of the device. After desorption, ethanol concentration was determined in the product. The air blower provided a closed cycle in which the adsorption and desorption took place. With the application of 7 kinds of GAC in this adsorption-desorption device an average ethanol content of 16.8 % from the 2 % stock solution was yielded in the product. In the case of the 5 % stock solution the product acquired an average ethanol concentration of 36 %. In some experiments, up to 9.7-times higher ethanol concentration was achieved in the product than at the beginning of the adsorption process.

articleTitle: Analysis of Educational Results of Ukrainian Students in Mathematics and Physics based on External Independent Assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article researches the educational outcomes of mathematics and physics students over the last 10 years based on the External Independent Assessment (EIA). External Independent Assessment is a test, that is make up by all applicants for higher education institutions to determine their educational performance, which is conducted and regulated by a unit of the Ministry of Education of Ukraine. The article deals with the correlations of interdisciplinary student achievement, the number of students and the level of knowledge by years.

articleTitle: Design and logistics of separate collection of municipal waste by underground containers
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Public interest in recycling has increased significantly over the past 15 years. This concern was initiated by several factors, such as concerns about increased waste production, the loss of landfill capacity, air pollution from waste incineration as well as the general recognition of the need for environmental protection. The authors of the article focused on the possibility of implementation of separate collection using underground containers. At the same time, the principles of separate collection in the European Union countries, in the Slovak Republic and in the city of Košice are analyzed. The authors designed a separate collection system and the logistics of the collection itself using underground containers. The proposal was processed for the city of Košice and its city district Košice KVP. The advantages and economic benefits of the present method of separate collection are presented.

articleTitle: Innovative Application Options of Sound Visualization Tools
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Sound visualization tools are powerful tools for identifying and locating noise sources. They are widely used in various sectors of industry. Noise visualization tools are often used for comprehensive knowledge of noise sources, which serves as a basis for subsequent implementation of noise reduction measures. They are also often used to optimize the acoustic properties of household appliances. A new area in the application of noise visualization tools is the area of building acoustics. At present, demands on acoustic parameters of building structures are increasing. Many people complain about the inadequate acoustic quality of the partition walls even in new buildings. Using visualization tools, it is possible to detect deficiencies in building structures such as perimeter walls, partition walls, roof structures and windows. This method is non-destructive and produces fast results. The result of such visualization is the precise identification of the critical points and their location. The most commonly used visualization tool is acoustic camera.

articleTitle: Assessment of the quality of ecological high-solid paints with low solvent content
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The paper presents the results of the research aimed at evaluating the quality of coatings based on ecological high solids paints with low content of solvents compared with classical synthetic paints. The quality of the selected coatings was evaluated by determining the adhesion of the coatings depending on the surface pretreatments used. The aim of the work was to determine the effect of pre-treatment on the adhesion of coatings and to evaluate the possibility of using a blasting media - almandine as a secondary raw material in the pre-treatment of steel surfaces. The adhesion of the coatings was determined by a grid test and a peel test. The quality of the pretreated surfaces was evaluated on the basis of changes in electrode potentials indoors and outdoors. Simulated Acid Rain Solution (SARS) was used as the electrolyte. The corrosion resistance of the coatings was evaluated by accelerated laboratory tests in an SO2-containing environment and by total immersion of the samples in a 20% NaCl solution. The environments were deliberately chosen to simulate the urban atmosphere. Following exposure of the test specimens, the change in coating.

articleTitle: Mathematical model for magnetic properties of materials in environmental engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Research and development in the field of environmental engineering technologies is expanding with an increasing interest in environmental protection, with which the closely related materials are used in the production and operation of frequently used industrial machinery and equipment. Such materials also include magnetic materials which are of particular importance for technical practice and are used in the construction of magnetic circuits, e.g. in generators, electric motors, transformers, core coils, various sensors, electromagnets, etc. Great emphasis is placed on saving electricity in the production, but also in the operation of equipment consisting of magnetic materials and the associated lower costs for the production process and also for more environmentally friendly recycling of materials.

articleTitle: Ukrainian After-School Education System: State and Topical Tendencies in the Development
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Review of state and topical tendencies in the development after-school education system in Ukraine. Filed of the efficient functioning of the after-school education in Ukraine is related to the normative and legal, organizational, personnel, scientific and methodical, financial and technical provision.

articleTitle: The role of sustainable development in the Environmental Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Nowadays all documents and studies related to sustainable development emphasize the need for a change of attitude and the responsibility of the universities for its implementation. Depend on this objective of environmental engineering BSc education is to develop competences like complex system approach, problem recognition and resolution, lifelong learning and responsible attitude for the environment in addition to high level scientific knowledge. To achieve this goal, besides professional academic training, environment education needs to be implemented, where project pedagogy -as the strategy of environment pedagogy-can be efficiently applied. The study aims to prove the effectiveness of project education in terms of professional knowledge as well as in environmental attitudes by the results of project and practical training with an ecological-minded. This paper elaborates a field practice in Aggtelek National Park, Hungary. Based on the results it can be stated, that project pedagogy and the field practice can be well integrated with traditional pedagogical methods and may become their efficient supplement in environmental engineering BSc education.

articleTitle: Competency-Based Approach in the After-School Education as Innovative Methods
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Review of the basic principles of after-school education with a competency-based approach. The main provisions on the competency approach and its use in after-school education in Ukraine are presented. The content and methodology of after-school education based on the competence approach have been developed. The main attention is paid to the realization of cognitive, practical, creative and social competences in the areas of after-school education.

articleTitle: Theory and Practice of Teaching Information Technology in After-School Education Institutions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article deals with the theory and practice of teaching information technology in after-school educational establishments. Theoretical foundations of information technology development are revealed, the main chronological stages of information technology formation and development are established. The current state of the information technology system is analyzed. The scientific substantiation of the methodological system of teaching information technologies in scientific and technical circles of after-school educational institutions is carried out. The purpose and content of teaching information technology students in after-school educational institutions are presented, organizational forms, methods and means are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of selected technologies of cable recycling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: With the rapid development of the power engineering, communication technology, utilisation of electronic products, automotive industry, the quantity of waste as wires or cables also increases. The colour metals, mainly copper and aluminium contained in the waste cables, have high purity and their recycling energy consumption is low. The aim of this contribution is to explore possibilities of recycling and sorting of electric cables, to summarize information about types of electric cables, their production and recycling. Given the large amount of cable waste, cable recycling is extremely important nowadays, not only from an environmental point of view, but also from an economic point of view. Based on this, the methodology of work and experiment was chosen, which describes methods of separation and recycling of electric cables. The laboratory methods of mechanical recycling were investigated. The advantages and disadvantages of recycling technology of waste cables will be analysed in the conclusion.

articleTitle: Zinc Removal from Waters by Hybrid Sorbent with Humic Acid
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Humic biogenic organics can promote the detoxification of aquatic ecosystems from heavy metal ions. However, humic acids have not been widely used in adsorptive remediation of natural waters because of high solubility. In the present article, we proposed hybrid adsorbent based on silica gel sequentially modified with a quaternary ammonium salt, tetradecylammonium nitrate, and humic acids and tested it for the removal of Zn(II) from the tap water. The maximum adsorption capacity of humic acids on the modified silica gel can reach 7.1 and 11.4 mg/g at pH 7 and 3.0, respectively. The immobilized humic acids are resistant to dissolution at pHs of 5-7 and different KCl concentrations. Elution of humic acids from sorbent at pH 5-7 is below 15%. Functional groups of immobilized humic acids can bind Zn(II) ions. By using the hybrid adsorbent, the removal of Zn(II) from aqueous solution reaches 94-97% at pH 5.0-6.0. We registered the H-type adsorption isotherm at a low initial concentration of Zn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions. The uptake of Zn(II) was relatively fast, and the equilibrium was reached for 20-25 min. The hybrid sorbent can be used to concentrate metal ions from natural waters and in water purification technologies.

articleTitle: Proposal for Disassembly of Electric Vehicle Batteries used in the Volkswagen Jetta Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Li-ion batteries (LIBs) are currently the most available and suitable energy storage device for powering electric vehicles (EVs) due to their wantable properties including high energy efficiency, lack of memory effect, high energy density, high power density and long life cycle. These advantages allow them to be smaller and lighter than other conventional rechargeable batteries such as lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium (Ni-Cd) and nickel-metal (Ni-MH) hybride batteries. The rising number of electric vehicles comes along with an increasing demand for LIBs. As resources such as lithium are valuable, it is economically desired to recycle EV batteries. One of the first steps of every battery recycling process is the disassembly, which can be a quite time and cost consuming process and hence has to be planned accurately and properly. Using the battery of the hybrid car Volkswagen Jetta Hybrid as a case study, a planning approach for the disassembly will be discussed in this paper. Therefore, disassembly sequences will be derived from a priority matrix and a disassembly graph will be drawn up. In fine, the design of the disassembly system and work stations will be recommended.

articleTitle: Soil Biological Parameters Inluenced by Various Nitrogen Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: Pot experiment was run out to study the impacts of different nitrogen sources on microbial biomass (C and N) and other soil biological properties in Kovarvany brown forest and meadow chernozem soil types incubated at temperature 25±3°C. Pots were filled up with soil amended with sewage sludge at the levels of 0, 12.5, 25, or 50% (w/w) in comparison with soil amended with ammonium nitrate at 0, 11.5, 23 and 46 mg/kg soil for eight weeks. The results were compared with a pot containing a combination between ammonium nitrate at 23 mg/kg soil mixed with 25% of sewage sludge and with untreated control. Soil aerobic heterotroph bacterial enumeration, fungal population, soil basal respiration, total soil organic carbon, dehydrogenase and fluorescein diacetic acid (FAD) potential activities were investigated. Results indicated that the addition of sludge or NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> caused changes in the sizes of microbial population which increased significantly with the increases of the application rates of organic N source (sewage sludge) more than the inorganic N source (NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>). In addition, sewage sludge had a stimulatory effect on the soil enzymatic potential activity and increases the total organic carbon. The highest number of fungi observed in meadow chernozem soil even treated with NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. It was found that Kovarvany brown forest soil had lower soil biomass and biological properties when treated with NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Moreover, meadow chernozem soil had higher biological properties when treated with sewage sludge than NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> over the Kovarvany brown forest soil. These results suggest that the positive correlation between organic fertilizer amendment and soil quality where enhance both microbial and enzymatic activities. However, the results indicated that soil enzyme activities have been proposed as appropriate indicators because of their intimate relationship to soil biology, ease of measurements, and rapid response to a small change in soil management.

articleTitle: Analysis of the separate collection of packaging waste from households in Slovakia in the context of Circular Economy Package
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The part of the EU Action Plan for the Circular Economy adopted by The European Commission is a result of revision of the waste legislative framework (so called Waste Package or Circular Economy Package). It includes measures to increase waste prevention, changes in product design, increase preparation for reuse and recycling, etc. The Waste Package, which contains revision of four directives, entered into force in July 2018 and the Member States have to transpose it by 2020. The revisions have introduced ambitious targets for municipal waste, packaging waste and a reduction in the amount of landfilled waste and they have established minimum requirements for extended producer responsibility (EPR). The main goal of this paper is to evaluate the separate collection of packaging waste from household in Slovakia in the context of Circular Economy Package.

articleTitle: Emission intensity of energy sector in V4 countries – decoupling analysis of GHG emissions and economic growth
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The production and use of energy satisfies human needs, but also gives rise to a host of adverse environmental pressures, such as air pollution or waste generation. The issue of energy efficiency and climate chance resonates in energy sector as one of the main producer of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. While the Union as a whole is doing well in reducing emissions as well as in increasing the share of renewables, unfortunately, there are countries still far from their goal. The aim of this paper is to quantitatively assess the relationship between economic growth of energy sector and production of GHG emissions by energy sector in the V4 countries using decoupling method. The paper focuses on the case of V4 countries in the period of 1995 - 2016. Throughout the more than 20 years examined, the countries spread out into many different forms of decoupling. The results of analysis suggest that in most observed partial variables occurs the strong decoupling of economic growth of energy sector (measured in GVA) and GHG emissions produced by energy sector, what can be considered as positive trend. Findings of the paper are relevant for government, state and public institutions as well as stakeholders in general who play important role in preparation of programs, projects and initiatives to make energy appliances, buildings, transport and energy generation more efficient, and introduces stringent new energy efficiency standards and financing mechanisms to support more energy efficient products.

articleTitle: Impact of Trifluralin and 2,4-D on Soil Microbial Biomass and Enzymatic Activities
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: An experiment was laid out in randomized block design with three replications under laboratory conditions to investigate the impacts of 2,4-D and Trifluralin applied at 0, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 mg/kg soil on total organic carbon (TOC), carbon dioxide release, microbial biomass carbon, enumeration of aerobic heterotrophic bacteria, fungal population and cellulose decomposers and enzymatic activities of fluorescein diacetic acid (FDA) and dehydrogenase activities in “kovarvany” brown forest (KBF, Nyíregyháza) and meadow chernozem (MC, Szeged) soil types incubated for 7 days at temperature 28°C. Results indicated that Trifluralin was more toxic than 2,4-D at higher concentrations. The findings of investigated parameters in MC soil type were higher than those obtained from KBF soil type under the stress of two tested herbicides. It was found that 10 mg/kg concentration more effective on the aerobic heterotrophic bacterial population and cellulose-decomposers than fungal population, FDA and dehydrogenase as well as TOC and CO2 production. Results showed that the application of herbicides at the tested levels were not drastic enough to be considered harmful to soil microbial and enzymatic activities which are important to soil fertility. This study has shown that the microbial activity increased as a result of adaptation to the herbicides during incubation period; also, demonstrates a potential capacity for adaptation of the microorganisms in soils when large amounts of herbicides are added. Dehydrogenase can consider as sensitive bioindicator of the microbial activity response to herbicidal amendment. More investigation can be done with different soil types under various ecological parameters.

articleTitle: Precision of the machine tool and its impact on the environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Council on Technologies of Environmental Protection (ICTEP)
abstract: The article describes the impact of the production process on the environment. Nowadays, humanity is already trying to minimize the negative impacts of production and the environment by introducing measures in every area of life. The article also deals with the accuracy of the machine tool - milling cutters. We chose the machining centre, where we tested the workpiece virtually and then practically milling, we made calculations in the positive and negative axes X, Y. The next step was measuring dynamic forces in materials and evaluating the measured results.
